title: Shital pati
summary: Plait a cool mat of fine cane strips and work a diamond medallion into its middle.
howToPlay: Look at the lit mat in its frame: it shows the pattern the finished mat must have.
Tap a colour to lay the next crossing along the row; the gold square marks the place, and the strip under the mat shows the row you are working on.
The strips not yet woven lie bare under the finished rows. Undo takes back the last crossing.
Press Check to see your stars, or Watch and learn to see a mat woven for you.
rules: Each crossing is laid in the colour you choose; rows run left to right, from the start of the work.
The weave goes over one, under one, a plain plait of cane.
The score counts the crossings that match the lit target, beyond what the plain fibre colour alone would give.
Undo takes back the last crossing.
Three stars for 88 or more, two stars for 65 and one star for 40.
Watch and learn plays a whole round for you.
heritageNote: In the Sylhet region of Bangladesh, weavers split murta cane into thin, smooth strips and plait them into mats. The name shital pati means cool mat: the glossy surface stays pleasant to sit and sleep on in the humid heat. Some strips are dyed, and the colours are worked into borders and central motifs.
